items.title: Police foil alleged terror attack plan on public buildings
items.description: Police have charged a 20-year-old man they allege was planning a "mass casualty" terror attack targeting public buildings and Muslim places of worship in Western Australia.

items.title: Bondi attackers embraced as 'soldiers' by Islamic State
items.description: Islamic State has embraced Sajid and Naveed Akram as "soldiers" and urged other supporters to continue attacks on Jews and Christians, as they claimed credit for the Bondi massacre.

items.title: Will Coles' bruising court battle be worth it?
items.description: Coles decided this bruising court battle was worth it and now a federal court judge is weighing up the evidence to decide whether that decision was a masterstroke or a massive error.

items.title: Clinton tells Congress he had 'no inkling' of Epstein's crimes
items.description: The former US president is being questioned by the House Oversight Committee, which is looking into the US government's handling of the Epstein case.

items.title: Once-in-a-generation deluge for SA and Vic as north eyes triple cyclone threat
items.description: There's the risk of dangerous flash flooding in populated regions stretching from Eyre Peninsula to western Victoria and the Murray River amid growing signs three additional tropical lows will form off Australia's northern coast next week.

items.title: Deputy chief of army warns ADF 'detached' from violent nature of war
items.description: Major General Chris Smith delivered an excoriating address to a major conference last year, declaring "managerial and advertising logic and double speak" had "polluted" the military.

items.title: Liberal Party won't publish its review into disastrous 2025 election
items.description: The review received hundreds of submissions and was finished months ago, but today the Liberal Party's federal executive revealed it would never be made public.

items.title: Traditional owners awarded $54m compensation for economic, spiritual loss
items.description: Native title holders in the Northern Territory have been awarded more than $54 million in compensation for the impacts of large-scale mining on their country, in just the second case of its kind in Australian history.

items.title: Towns cut off, cars swept away in extreme weather across the country
items.description: At least four states are facing extreme weather and heavy rain, with some areas tipped to receive the heaviest rainfall in more than a decade.

items.title: 'My whole licence gone': Drivers caught unaware by AI traffic cameras
items.description: WA drivers given large fines or a licence suspension after their passengers were snapped wearing seatbelts incorrectly say they are being punished for behaviour beyond their control.

items.title: Expert warning after man, dog struck by lightning in freak storm
items.description: After a day that saw 10,000 lightning strikes across Perth, three people suffer injuries, and a pet dog killed, an expert shares tips for avoiding injury during electrical storms.

items.title: Ex-SA Liberal leader says he will contest election, 10 months after drug conviction
items.description: Former SA Liberal leader David Speirs has confirmed he has nominated to run in his former seat of Black in the state election, 10 months after he was convicted of drug supply offences.

items.title: Pakistan declares 'open war' against Afghanistan as Kabul hit by air strikes
items.description: Pakistan is responding to "unprovoked fire" by Afghan forces at multiple locations along the border, the Information Ministry in Islamabad says.

items.title: Unexpected birth of a boy brings hope for Amazonian tribe with no men
items.description: As they advanced in age without a child to carry on the line, many expected the Akuntsu to vanish when the three remaining women died.

items.title: Basic habits to help young people be financially resilient
items.description: Many people are struggling with the cost of living and increasingly, young Australians say they are not just worried about the situation now, but also what it means for the future.

items.title: Almost 40,000 Budget Direct customers overcharged, ASIC takes legal action
items.description: The corporate regulator is taking legal action over allegations Budget Direct customers lost online discounts they were promised and were overcharged.

items.title: The 11 books our critics couldn't put down this summer
items.description: Wondering what to read next? Buzzy debuts, gripping thrillers and lyrical literary fiction are among our critics' latest recommendations.

items.title: Coroner hears of string of maintenance failures before 3yo's house fire death
items.description: The inquest into three-year-old Mitchell Thomas's death in an Alice Springs house fire in 2023 has finished hearing evidence, with the coroner examining standards of maintenance, record-keeping and electrical safety regulation in the NT's public housing.

items.title: Protestor arrested as NT administrator sworn in despite social media posts
items.description: A protester has been arrested amid chaotic scenes outside of NT Parliament, where David Connolly has been sworn in as the new administrator.

items.title: Katrina Gorry has done it all for the Matildas. Now she wants a trophy
items.description: Katrina Gorry embodies all the characteristics that are celebrated in Australian football, and the veteran midfielder wants to lead the Matildas all the way to the Asian Cup trophy.

items.title: Reds pull out trick shots on victorious day for Australian Super Rugby
items.description: The Queensland Reds and Western Force have recorded their first wins of the Super Rugby Pacific season in round three.

items.title: Young gun blazes century as Australia takes charge of India series
items.description: Georgia Voll strikes her second ODI century after being dropped on 99, as Australia cruises to a five-wicket win over India and takes a 6-4 lead in the multi-format series.

items.title: What to check out this weekend: Gorillaz, Chris Fleming and a pasta salad
items.description: Looking for something diverting for the weekend? We've got you covered.

items.title: Darwin fashion label founder faces court on domestic violence charges
items.description: The founder of popular fashion label House of Darwin has faced court on assault, choking, and strangling charges after an alleged domestic violence incident last year.

items.title: Mitch Brown came out six months ago. Now he's co-hosting Mardi Gras parade
items.description: Just six months since coming out, ex-AFL player Mitch Brown is now co-hosting Sydney's Mardi Gras parade. He hopes his journey can help other players embrace who they are.
